Surah Al 'Imran [Madaniyya; its verses are two hundred, or except one verse; it was revealed after al-Anfal]

﴿Alif Lam Mim﴾ Allah knows best what He means by this.

Revealed to you, O Muhammad, is the Book, the Qur'an, in truth, meaning with truthfulness in its reports, confirming what is before it, meaning the books before it. And He revealed the Torah and the Gospel before this, meaning before its revelation, as a guidance, a circumstantial state (ḥāl) in the sense of "guiding," from misguidance, for the people, meaning for those who followed them. He used the verb "anzala" (sent down) for the two, and "nazzala" (sent down gradually) for the Qur'an, which implies repetition, because the two were sent down all at once, unlike it. And He sent down the Criterion (al-Furqān), in the sense of the books that distinguish between truth and falsehood. He mentioned it after mentioning the three so that it would include whatever else there is.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 4:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾ (the Qur'an and other than it), ﴿will have a severe punishment. And Allah is Exalted in Might﴾ (dominant over His affair), so nothing prevents Him from carrying out His promise and His threat, ﴿Owner of Retribution﴾ (a severe punishment) against whoever disobeys Him, the like of which no one can inflict.

Indeed, Allah – nothing is hidden from Him ﴿on the earth or in the heaven﴾ that exists, because of His knowledge of what occurs in the world, both universal and particular. He specified these two [the earth and the heaven] by mention because the senses do not extend beyond them.
He is the One who forms you in the wombs however He wills: male or female, white or black, and other than that. ﴿There is no god but Him, the Almighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His creation.

He it is who has sent down to you the Book. In it are verses that are **muhkamat** (*muhkam*: definite, clear in their indication), and they are the mother of the Book, its fundamental basis on which rulings are relied. And others are **mutashabihat** (*mutashabih*: ambiguous), whose meanings are not understood, such as the opening letters of the surahs. He described the whole of it as muhkam in His saying, ﴿its verses have been made firm﴾, meaning that there is no defect in it. He described it as mutashabih in His saying, ﴿a Book whose parts are similar to one another﴾, meaning that parts of it resemble one another in excellence and truthfulness. ﴿As for those in whose hearts is deviation﴾, meaning inclination away from the truth, ﴿they follow what is ambiguous of it, seeking﴾, meaning desiring, ﴿discord﴾, due to their ignorance, by their falling into doubtful matters and confusion, ﴿and seeking its **ta'wil** (interpretation)﴾, meaning its *tafsir* (explanation). ﴿And none knows its ta'wil except Allah﴾ alone. ﴿And those firmly rooted in knowledge﴾, meaning those who are steadfast and well-established, ﴿say: "We believe in it"﴾, meaning in the mutashabih, that it is from the presence of Allah, and we do not know its meaning. ﴿All of it is from our Lord﴾, meaning both the muhkam and the mutashabih. ﴿And none takes heed except those of understanding﴾, meaning those possessing intellects; the verb *yadhdhakkaru* is originally *yatadhakkaru*, with the ta' (ت) assimilated (*idgham*) into the dhal (ذ), meaning: takes admonition. And they also say, when they see those who follow it:

﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate﴾ by turning them away from the truth through seeking an interpretation (ta'wil) of it that is not fitting for us, as You turned away the hearts of those [others] ﴿after You had guided us﴾ to it, ﴿and grant us mercy from Yourself﴾ from Your presence, [mercy] for steadfastness, ﴿indeed You are the Bestower﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 9:

O ﴿our Lord, indeed You are the Gatherer of the people﴾ You will gather them ﴿for a Day﴾, i.e., on a day ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾, no uncertainty ﴿in it﴾. It is the Day of Resurrection, so You will recompense them for their deeds, as You promised that. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise﴾, His promise of resurrection in it. There is a shift (iltifat) from address (khitab) here, and it is possible that it is part of the speech of Allah the Exalted, and the purpose of supplicating with this is to make clear that their concern is the matter of the Hereafter, and therefore they asked for steadfastness upon guidance so that they might attain its reward. Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: (The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: "He it is who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are precise (muhkamat)..." to its end, and said: "When you see those who follow what is unclear (mutashabih) of it, those are the ones whom Allah has named, so beware of them.") Al-Tabarani in al-Kabir narrated from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: (I fear for my Ummah only three qualities..." and he mentioned among them: that the Book will be opened to them, so the believer takes it seeking its interpretation (ta'wil), while no one knows its interpretation except Allah, and those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rasikhun fi al-'ilm) say: "We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord," and none takes heed except those of understanding (ulu al-albab)." The hadith continues.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 10:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth will not avail them, nor their children, against Allah at all﴾ [i.e., it will not repel (تَدْفَع) from them] ﴿Allah's punishment﴾ [i.e., His punishment] ﴿in any way﴾ ﴿And those are the fuel (وَقُود, waqud) of the Fire﴾ [with the waw pronounced with a fatḥa (وَقُودُ النَّار), meaning that with which it is kindled (ما تُوقَد بِهِ)].

Their custom is ﴿like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them﴾ among the nations, such as ʿAd and Thamud. ﴿They denied Our signs, so Allah seized them﴾ — He destroyed them — ﴿for their sins﴾. The clause is explanatory of what precedes it. ﴿And Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

It was revealed when the Prophet (ﷺ) called the Jews to Islam after his return from Badr. They said: "Do not let it deceive you that you killed a band of Quraysh, novices who do not know how to fight."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 12:

﴿Say﴾ (O Muhammad) to ﴿those who disbelieve﴾ — from among the Jews — ﴿You will be overcome﴾ (read with both the ta' and the ya'), in this world, by killing, captivity, and the imposition of the jizya (poll-tax); and this has indeed happened. ﴿And you will be gathered﴾ (read with both readings) ﴿to Hell﴾ in the Hereafter, so that you will enter it, ﴿and wretched is the resting-place﴾, the bed it is.

﴿There has indeed been for you a sign﴾, meaning a lesson (ʿibrah). The verb is given in the masculine form, كان (kāna), for separation (al-faṣl), since the word آية (āyah) is feminine but is separated from its verb. ﴿In two groups﴾, meaning two companies, ﴿that met﴾ on the Day of Badr for battle: ﴿one group fighting in the way of Allah﴾, meaning in obedience to Him. They were the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, who numbered three hundred and thirteen men. With them were two horses, six coats of mail, and eight swords, and most of them were on foot. ﴿And another, disbelieving group, who saw them﴾, meaning the unbelievers, ﴿as twice their number﴾, meaning the Muslims, that is, they saw the unbelievers as more than double the Muslims, and the unbelievers numbered about a thousand. ﴿With their own eyes﴾, meaning a clear, direct sight. Allah nevertheless granted them victory despite their small number. ﴿And Allah strengthens﴾, meaning supports, ﴿with His help whom He wills. Indeed in that﴾, the aforementioned event, ﴿is a lesson for those who have insight﴾, meaning for those who possess understanding. Will you not then take heed from this and believe?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 14:

﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires﴾ — what the soul desires and calls to; Allah beautified it as a trial, or it was beautified by the Devil. ﴿Of women, sons, and heaped-up piles of gold and silver﴾ — the abundant wealth ﴿heaped up﴾ — gathered together ﴿of gold and silver, and branded horses﴾ — the fine ones, ﴿and livestock﴾ — that is, camels, cattle, and sheep, ﴿and tilth﴾ — crops. ﴿That﴾ — the aforementioned — ﴿is the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾ — one enjoys it therein, then it perishes. ﴿But with Allah is the best return﴾ — the place of return, which is Paradise, so one should desire it above anything else.

Say, [O Muhammad, to your people]: "Shall I inform you of something better than that [which has been mentioned of desires]?" The interrogative here is for affirmation (istifham taqrir). "For those who have feared [shirk]: with their Lord are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein" (khalidina), meaning destined to abide eternally "therein" when they enter them, "and purified spouses" (azwaj mutahharah), purified from menstruation and other things that are considered repugnant, "and approval" (ridwan), which is read with a kasra or a damma on its first letter, both being dialects, meaning abundant approval "from Allah. And Allah is Seeing" (basir), knowing "of the servants," so He will recompense each of them according to his deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 16:

﴿Alladhīna﴾ is an adjectival qualifier (naʿt) or an apposition (badal) of the preceding ﴿alladhīna﴾. ﴿Yaqūlūna﴾ (they say), "﴿Rabbanā innanā āmannā﴾" (O our Lord, indeed we have believed), meaning: we have affirmed (ṣaddaqnā) You and Your Messenger. ﴿Fa-ghfir lanā dhunūbanā wa-qinā ʿadhāba l-nār﴾ (so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire).

Translation of the passage:

﴿The patient﴾ in obedience and in abstaining from disobedience, an adjective (naʿt). ﴿The truthful﴾ in faith. ﴿The obedient﴾ (al-qānitīn), those who obey God. ﴿The spenders﴾ (al-munfiqīn), those who give charity. ﴿Those who seek forgiveness﴾ from God, by saying, "O God, forgive us." ﴿At the dawn﴾ (bil-asḥār), the last part of the night. It was singled out for mention because it is the time of heedlessness and the pleasure of sleep.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 18:

﴿Allah bears witness﴾ He makes clear to His creation, by the proofs and signs, ﴿that there is no god﴾ (ilah), i.e., no one worthy of worship in existence in truth, ﴿except Him﴾. He bears witness to this, ﴿and the angels﴾ by affirmation, ﴿and those of knowledge﴾ from among the prophets and the believers, by belief and utterance, ﴿standing﴾ in the management of His creatures, and it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), and its governing element is the meaning of the sentence, i.e., He is singular ﴿in justice﴾ (qist), i.e., in equity. ﴿There is no god except Him﴾ — He repeated it for emphasis. ﴿The Mighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His making.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 19:

﴿Indeed, the religion﴾ acceptable ﴿with Allah﴾ is ﴿Islam﴾, i.e., the law brought by the messengers, founded upon monotheism. In another reading, "that" (anna) is vowed with a fatḥah, in apposition to "that He" (annahu) etc., as an apposition of inclusion (badal ishtimal). ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not differ﴾, namely the Jews and the Christians, concerning the religion, in that some affirmed monotheism and some disbelieved, ﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾ of monotheism, ﴿out of envy﴾ (baghyan) from the disbelievers ﴿among themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah﴾ ﴿—indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾, i.e., in recompense for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 20:

﴿Then if they dispute with you﴾ the disbelievers dispute with you, O Muhammad, concerning the religion, ﴿then say﴾ to them: ﴿I have submitted my face to God, and whoever follows me﴾ I have surrendered to Him, I, ﴿and whoever follows me﴾. He specified the face for mention because of its nobility, so other parts [of the body] are more fitting [for submission]. ﴿And say to those who were given the Book﴾ the Jews and the Christians, ﴿and to the unlettered﴾ the polytheists of the Arabs, ﴿Have you submitted?﴾ meaning: submit! ﴿If they submit, then they have been guided﴾ from error, ﴿but if they turn away﴾ from Islam, ﴿then upon you is only the conveyance﴾ meaning the delivery of the message, ﴿and God is Seeing of [His] servants﴾ so He will recompense them for their deeds. And this was before the command to fight.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 21:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right, and kill those who enjoin justice from among the people﴾ — in another reading, "yuqatilun" (fight) instead of "yaqtulun" (kill) — ﴿...﴾ "bil-qist" means "bil-'adl" (with justice), ﴿from among the people﴾, and they are the Jews. It is narrated that they killed forty-three prophets, then a hundred and seventy of their worshippers forbade them, and they killed them on the same day. ﴿So give them tidings﴾, i.e., inform them, ﴿of a painful punishment﴾, i.e., painful. Mentioning "tidings" is a form of mockery toward them. The "fa'" (fa, "so") has entered the predicate of "inna" because its relative-pronoun subject resembles the conditional (shart).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 22:

﴿Those are they whose deeds have become void﴾ (baṭalat), ﴿their works﴾ — whatever good they did, such as charity and maintaining ties of kinship — ﴿in this world and the Hereafter﴾; so they are not credited for them, since the condition for them (i.e., faith) is absent. ﴿And they will have no helpers﴾, i.e., no ones who will prevent them from the punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 23:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ look at (tanzur) ﴿those who were given a portion﴾ a share (ḥaẓẓan) ﴿of the Book﴾ the Torah (al-Tawrah) ﴿who are invited﴾ a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) ﴿to the Book of Allah, that it may judge between them, and then a faction of them turn away﴾ ﴿while they are refusing﴾ from accepting its judgment. It was revealed concerning the Jews: two of them committed adultery, so they brought their dispute to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he ruled that they be stoned. They refused, so the Torah was brought and they found the ruling in it, and they were stoned, and they became angry.

That (turning away and refusal) is because they said, meaning, because of their saying: "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days," forty days, the period during which their fathers worshipped the calf, after which it will leave them. "And what they used to fabricate deceived them in their religion," this phrase is connected to "what they used to fabricate," i.e., of their saying that.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 25:**

﴿Then how⦆ will be their condition ﴿when We gather them for a Day⦆, that is, on a day, ﴿about which there is no doubt⦈, no uncertainty ﴿concerning it⦈; it is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and every soul will be paid in full⦈ for what it has earned, from the People of the Book and others, the recompense of ﴿what it earned⦈, of good and evil ﴿and they will not be wronged⦈ by any reduction of a good deed or any addition to an evil deed.

Revealed when the Prophet (ﷺ) promised his community the kingdoms of Persia and Byzantium, and the hypocrites said, "Far-fetched!" (hayhat):

﴿Say: "O Allah, Master of the Kingdom"﴾ O Allah, ﴿You give the kingdom﴾ (tu'ti, i.e., You bestow) ﴿to whom You will﴾ of Your creation, ﴿and You take the kingdom away from whom You will, and You exalt whom You will﴾ by granting it to him, ﴿and You abase whom You will﴾ by removing it from him, ﴿in Your hand﴾ (bi-yadika), that is, by Your power, ﴿is the good﴾ (al-khayr), i.e., and the evil, ﴿indeed You are over all things competent.﴾

ﷻ﻿ ﴿You cause the night to pass into the day﴾ (tūlij) ﴿tudkhil﴾ "You make enter", ﴿the night into the day﴾ and ﴿You cause the day to pass into the night﴾ ﴿tudkhilu﴾ "You make it enter", ﴿into the night﴾, so each of them gains what the other has lost. ﴿You bring the living out of the dead﴾ like a human being and a bird from a drop of semen and an egg, ﴿and You bring the dead out of the living﴾ like the drop of semen and the egg ﴿out of the living﴾, ﴿and You provide for whom You will without reckoning﴾, i.e., abundant provision.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 28:

﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies﴾ (yuwaluna-hum, i.e., they befriend them) ﴿instead of the believers﴾ (ay, other than the believers). ﴿And whoever does that﴾ (ay, befriends them) ﴿has nothing to do with Allah's religion﴾ (din, religion) ﴿in any way, unless you fear them as a precaution﴾ (taqiyyah, the verbal noun of taqaytuhu, i.e., you fear a fear), ﴿for then you may show friendship to them with your tongues, not your hearts. This was before Islam became strong, and it applies to whoever is in a land where he is not powerful.﴾ ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾ (yukhawwifukum, i.e., He makes you fear) ﴿that He may become angry with you if you befriend them﴾ ﴿and to Allah is the final return﴾ (al-maṣīr, the place of return), ﴿so He will recompense you.﴾

Say (to them): "Whether you conceal what is in your breasts (qulubukum, your hearts, concerning your alliance with them) or disclose it (tuzhirūhu, you make it manifest), Allah knows it, and He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and Allah is over all things Competent (qadir)." Among that is the punishment of those who befriended them.

Remember (the Day when every soul finds what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil; it wishes that between it and that were a far-off distance) — the phrase "what it has done of evil" is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is "it wishes that between it and it were a far-off distance," meaning an extreme distance, so that it never reaches it. "And Allah warns you of Himself" — this is repeated for emphasis. "And Allah is Compassionate to His servants."

It was revealed when they said, "We worship the idols only out of love for God, so that they may bring us near to Him." ﴿Say﴾ (to them, O Muhammad): ﴿If you love God, then follow me; God will love you﴾, meaning, will reward you, ﴿and forgive you your sins. And God is Forgiving﴾ to whoever follows me, of what has passed from him before that, ﴿Merciful﴾ to him.

Say [to them]: "Obey Allah and the Messenger," in what He commands you of monotheism. "But if they turn away," i.e., turn away from obedience, "then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers." In this there is the placing of the apparent noun in the position of the pronoun; that is, He does not love them, meaning that He punishes them.

Indeed, Allah chose (اصطفى, ṣṭafā: He selected, chose) ﴿Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImrān﴾ over ﴿the worlds﴾ (ʿālamīn), in the sense of their selves (ʿalā al-ʿālamīn, i.e. their persons), by making the prophets from their offspring.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on Surah 3, verse 34:

﴿Offspring, one of another﴾ (ﷺ) — the offspring of some of them from others.

Wait, let me translate that accurately. The passage reads:

﴿ذُرِّيَّة بَعْضها مِن﴾ ولَد ﴿بَعْض﴾ مِنهُمْ

Translation:

﴿Offspring, one of another﴾ — a child of one another among them.

Mention (O Muhammad) when the wife of Imran (Hannah), after she had grown old and longed for a child, said, and she prayed to God and sensed the pregnancy: "My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb to be dedicated (muharraran), freed (ʿatiqan), purified from the preoccupations of the world, for the service of Your Holy House. So accept it from me. Indeed You are the All-Hearing of the supplication, the All-Knowing of the intentions." And Imran died while she was pregnant.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 36:

﴿So when she gave birth to her﴾ she gave birth to a female child, and she had been hoping it would be a boy, since only boys were dedicated (to the service of the temple). ﴿She said﴾ apologetically: O ﴿my Lord, I have given birth to her,﴾ ﴿and Allah knows best﴾ i.e., knows ﴿what she has given birth to.﴾ The phrase is a parenthetical interjection from the speech of Allah, Exalted is He. In another reading, the taʾ is vowelled with a ḍammah (wa-llāhu aʿlamu bi-mā wuḍaʿat, "and Allah knows best what she has given birth to"). ﴿And the male is not like the female﴾ that I asked for ﴿that I have been given,﴾ because the male is intended for service, and she is not fit for it due to her weakness, her nakedness (ʿawrah), and what befalls her of menstruation and the like. ﴿And I have named her Maryam, and I seek refuge for her with You, and for her offspring,﴾ their children, ﴿from Satan the accursed,﴾ the one who has been driven away. In the hadith: "No child is born except that Satan touches it at the moment of its birth, so it cries out loudly, except Maryam and her son." Related by al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 3, verse 37:

﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance﴾, i.e., He accepted Maryam from her mother ﴿with a good acceptance, and made her grow with a good growth﴾, He brought her up with good character. So she would grow in a day as a child grows in a year. Her mother brought her to the rabbis (al-Ahbar), the custodians (sadanah) of the House of the Holy Place (Bayt al-Maqdis), and said: "Take this consecrated girl (al-nadhirah)," and they competed for her, because she was the daughter of their imam. Zakariyya said: "I am most entitled to her, because her maternal aunt is with me." They said: "No, let us draw lots." So they set out, twenty-nine of them, to the river Jordan (Nahr al-Urdunn), and they cast their pens (aqlam) on the condition that whoever's pen remained standing in the water and rose up would be the most entitled to her. Zakariyya's pen remained standing, so he took her and built for her a chamber (ghurfah) in the mosque, with a ladder that no one else could climb up to her. He would bring her her food, drink and oil, and he would find with her summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer, as He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And Zakariyya took charge of her﴾, i.e., he took her into his care (dammaha ilayhi). In another reading, it is read with the shaddah and with Zakariyya in the accusative, with the long and short vowel, and the subject is Allah. ﴿Whenever Zakariyya entered upon her in the sanctuary (al-mihrab)﴾, the chamber, and it is the most noble of the places of assembly, ﴿he found with her provision. He said: "O Maryam, from where﴾ (anna) ﴿is this for you?" She said﴾, while she was a little girl, ﴿"It is from Allah." Indeed Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾, i.e., abundant provision without accountability.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 38:

﴿There﴾ (hunalika), meaning: when Zakariyya saw that, and knew that the One who is able to bring about a thing outside its time is able to bring about a child in old age, and his family had died out, ﴿Zakariyya called upon his Lord﴾ when he entered the prayer niche (mihrab) for prayer in the depth of the night, ﴿saying: My Lord, grant me from Yourself﴾, meaning, from Your presence, ﴿a good offspring﴾, meaning a righteous son, ﴿You are Hearer﴾, meaning One who answers, ﴿of supplication﴾.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 3, verse 39:

﴿Then the angels called him﴾, i.e., Jibril, ﴿while he was standing in prayer in the mihrab﴾, i.e., the masjid, ﴿that﴾, i.e., that (Allah) ﴿Allah gives you good news﴾ — read with the doubled and the single-consonant forms — ﴿of Yahya, confirming a word﴾ coming ﴿from Allah﴾, i.e., of Isa, that he is a spirit of Allah; and he was called "a word" because he was created by the word "Be" (kun). ﴿And a master﴾, one who is followed, ﴿and chaste﴾, one restrained from women, ﴿and a prophet from among the righteous.﴾ It is narrated that he never committed a sin nor even intended one.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 40:

﴿He said: "My Lord, how can I have a boy when old age has already reached me and my wife is barren?"﴾ How (kayfa) will there be for me a son (ghulam), that is, a child? ﴿Old age has already reached me﴾, meaning I have reached the extreme of age, one hundred and twenty years. ﴿And my wife is barren﴾, she has reached ninety-eight years. ﴿He said: "So it is"﴾, the matter is ﴿thus﴾, by the creation of Allah, a boy from you both. ﴿Allah does what He wills﴾, nothing can incapacitate Him from it. And to manifest this great power, He inspired him to ask the question so that it might be answered with it, and because his soul yearned for the speedy fulfilment of the good news given to him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 41:

﴿He said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign"﴾ i.e., a sign (ʿalamah) of my wife's conception. ﴿He said: "Your sign"﴾ that it has occurred ﴿is that you will not speak to the people for three days﴾ i.e., you will refrain from speaking to them, unlike the remembrance of God Most High. ﴿Except by gesture﴾ (ramzan), meaning signaling. ﴿And remember your Lord much and glorify [Him]﴾ i.e., pray (ṣalli) ﴿in the evening and the morning﴾ i.e., the last and first parts of the day.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 42:

﴿And﴾ remember ﴿when the angels said﴾, i.e., Jibril, ﴿"O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you﴾, i.e., selected you, ﴿and purified you﴾ from the touch of men, ﴿and chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾, i.e., the women of your time.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 43:

﴿O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾ obey Him, ﴿and prostrate yourself and bow with those who bow﴾ i.e., pray with those who pray.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 44:

﴿That﴾, the matter mentioned concerning Zakariyya and Maryam, ﴿is among the tidings of the unseen﴾, the reports of what is hidden from you, ﴿which We reveal to you﴾, O Muhammad. ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens﴾ into the water, drawing lots, so that it would become clear to them ﴿which of them would take charge of﴾, would raise, ﴿Maryam. And you were not with them when they disputed﴾ over her guardianship, so that you would know that and inform of it; rather, you knew it through revelation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 45:

﴿When the angels said﴾, that is, Jibril, ﴿"O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good news of a word from Him﴾, that is, a child, ﴿whose name is al-Masih ʿIsa son of Maryam﴾. He addressed her by ascribing him to her, as a reminder that she would bear him without a father, since it is the custom of men to be ascribed to their fathers. ﴿Honored (wajih)﴾, having standing (jah) ﴿in this world﴾ through prophethood, ﴿and the Hereafter﴾ through intercession and the high ranks, ﴿and of those brought near﴾ to Allah.

{Wa yukallimu al-nasa fi al-mahd} means: speaking to people in the cradle, i.e., as an infant before the time of speech (ṭifلan qabl waqt al-kalam). {Wa kahlan wa min al-ṣāliḥīn} ...

Let me give that properly, since the passage must be translated faithfully:

﴿And he will speak to the people in the cradle﴾, that is, as an infant before the time of speech, ﴿and as a man of maturity, and he will be among the righteous﴾.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 3, verse 47:

﴿She said: "My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me?"﴾ How (kayfa) will there be a child for me, when no man has touched me, by marriage or otherwise? ﴿He said: "So it is."﴾ The matter is thus: creation of a child from you without a father. ﴿God creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ That is, when He wills to create it. ﴿So it is that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ I.e., so it comes to be.
﴿And He will teach him﴾ with the nūn (بِالنُّون) and the yā' (وَالياء), ﴿the Book﴾ meaning the writing (الخَطّ), ﴿and the wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel﴾.

And [He will make him] a messenger to the Children of Israel. This was either in his childhood or after reaching maturity. Then Gabriel blew into the opening of her shift, and she conceived. What happened to her is as mentioned in Surah Maryam. When God sent him to the Children of Israel, he said to them: "Indeed, I am God's messenger to you," [saying] ﴿that I﴾, i.e., "that I ﴿have come to you with a sign﴾" (a sign, proof of my truthfulness) ﴿from your Lord﴾, which is ﴿that I﴾. In another reading, with a kasra on the *alif* of *anni*, it is a resumed sentence (*isti'naf*, a new sentence that does not depend grammatically on what precedes it). ﴿I create﴾, i.e., I shape ﴿for you from clay the likeness of a bird﴾, resembling its form. The *kaf* here is an object of the verb in the passive sense (*ism maf'ul*, the passive participle form, meaning "that which is shaped"). ﴿Then I breathe into it﴾, where the pronoun refers to the *kaf* (the likeness). ﴿And it becomes a bird﴾; in another reading it is *ta'iran* (a living bird). ﴿By God's permission﴾, i.e., by His will. So He created for them a bat, because it is the most complete of birds in its creation, and it would fly while they watched it. When it went out of their sight, it fell down dead. ﴿And I heal﴾, i.e., I cure ﴿the blind from birth﴾, who was born blind, ﴿and the leper﴾. These two were singled out for mention because they are the two most difficult afflictions to treat. His mission took place in an age of medicine, and he healed fifty thousand people in a single day by supplication, on condition of faith. ﴿And I raise the dead by God's permission﴾. He repeated this phrase to deny any suspicion of divinity in him. He raised Azar, a friend of his, the son of an old woman, and the daughter of the tenth man, and they lived and had children. He also raised Sam, the son of Noah, who died immediately [afterward]. ﴿And I tell you what you eat and what you store﴾, i.e., hide ﴿in your houses﴾, of what I have not witnessed. He would inform a person of what he had eaten and what he would eat afterward. ﴿Surely in that﴾, the aforementioned, ﴿is a sign for you, if you are believers﴾.

﴿And﴾ I have come to you "confirming what was before me" of the Torah, "and to make lawful for you some of that which was forbidden to you" therein. So He made lawful for them, of fish and birds, that which has no ṣiṣṣa (a spur or claw). It was also said that He made all of it lawful, so "some" (baʿḍ) is in the sense of "all" (kull). ﴿And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord﴾: he repeated it for emphasis and so that what follows is built upon it. ﴿So fear God and obey me﴾ in what I command you of the tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) of God and of obeying Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 51:

﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this﴾ [is] that which I enjoin upon you, ﴿is a straight path﴾ [i.e., a way] ﴿straight﴾. Yet they denied him and did not believe in him.

When Jesus sensed their disbelief (﴿فَلَمّا أحَسَّ﴾), he knew (﴿عِيسى مِنهُمْ الكُفْر﴾) that they intended to kill him. He said, "Who are my helpers (anṣārī) on the way to God (﴿إلى اللَّه﴾)?" That is, going forth to God, to support His religion. (﴿قالَ مَن أنْصارِي﴾ أعْوانِي ذاهِبًا ﴿إلى اللَّه﴾ لِأَنْصُر دِينه) The disciples (al-ḥawāriyyūn) said, "We are God's helpers (﴿نَحْنُ أنْصار اللَّه﴾), the helpers of His religion. They were Jesus's chosen companions (aṣfiyā'), the first to believe in him, and they were twelve men from al-ḥūr, which is pure white. It was also said that they were launderers who whiten clothes, that is, they make them white." (﴿قالَ الحَوارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أنْصار اللَّه﴾ أعْوان دِينه وهُمْ أصْفِياء عِيسى أوَّل مَن آمَنَ بِهِ وكانُوا اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ رَجُلًا مِن الحُور وهُوَ البَياض الخالِص وقِيلَ كانُوا قَصّارِينَ يَحُورُونَ الثِّياب أيْ يُبَيِّضُونَها) They said, "We have believed in God (﴿آمَنّا بِاللَّهِ﴾), that is, we have affirmed Him. And bear witness, O Jesus, (﴿واشْهَدْ يا عِيسى﴾) that we are Muslims (﴿بأنا مسلمون﴾)."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 53:

﴿Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down﴾ from the Gospel, ﴿and we have followed the Messenger﴾ Jesus, ﴿so register us among the witnesses﴾ to Your oneness, and to the truthfulness of Your Messenger.

Almighty God said: ﴿And they schemed﴾, that is, the disbelievers among the Children of Israel against Jesus, when they appointed someone to kill him secretly. ﴿And God schemed﴾ against them, by casting the likeness of Jesus upon the one who intended to kill him, so they killed him; and Jesus was raised up to heaven. ﴿And God is the best of schemers﴾, the most knowing of them in it.

Remember when God said: "O Jesus, I am going to take you in full (mutawaffīka), that is, I will take you (qābiḍuka, seize you), and raise you to Me" from the world, without death; "and purify you" (muṭahhiruka), that is, remove you "from those who disbelieve"; "and make those who follow you" who affirmed your prophethood "superior to those who disbelieve" in you, namely the Jews, "over them" (ya'lūnahum) by argument and by the sword, "until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me will be your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ" regarding matters of religion.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 56:

﴿As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers﴾ — by killing, taking captives, and the jizya (poll-tax); "and in the Hereafter" — ﴿with the Fire﴾ — "and they will have no helpers" — ﴿preventing it from them﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 57:

﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full﴾ [read with the ya' and the nun, i.e., "fa-yuwaffihim" in both readings]. ﴿And Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., He will punish them. It is narrated that Allah sent a cloud to him (Jesus), which lifted him up, and his mother clung to him and wept. He said to her: "Indeed, the Resurrection will gather us together." This occurred on the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr) at Bayt al-Maqdis, and he was thirty-three years old. His mother lived six years after him. Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated the hadith: "He will descend near the Hour, judge by the law of our Prophet, kill the Dajjal and the swine, break the cross, and abolish the jizyah." In the hadith of Muslim, it is said that he will remain for seven years; and in a hadith from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, forty years. He will die and be prayed over. So it is possible that what is meant is the total of his stay on earth before the raising and after it.

﴿That﴾ refers to what has been mentioned about the matter of ʿĪsā (Jesus), ﴿We recite it﴾ i.e., We relate it ﴿to you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿of the signs﴾. It is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative, a grammatical term meaning a phrase describing the state of another noun) from the pronoun in *natlūhu*, and its governing element is the sense of pointing (*al-ishāra*) contained in *dhālika*. ﴿And the wise reminder﴾, i.e., the muḥkam (the firmly established, decisive), which is the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 59:

﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus﴾, his remarkable state, ﴿with Allah is like the likeness of Adam﴾, whose state in his creation was similar, from without a father. This is a comparison of the strange to the stranger, so that it is more decisive against the opponent and more striking to the soul. ﴿He created him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was﴾, a human being, ﴿and he was﴾, i.e., so he came to be. Likewise Jesus: He said to him, "Be," without a father, and he came to be.

Qur'anic quotations (within ﴿ ﴾) keep markers; translate meaning.

﴿The truth is from your Lord﴾, a predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada'), i.e., the matter of ʿIsa (Jesus). ﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾, those who are in doubt concerning it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 61:

﴿Whoever argues with you﴾ about it (i.e., about Jesus) from the Christians ﴿after the knowledge has come to you﴾ concerning his affair, ﴿then say﴾ to them: ﴿Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves﴾, then we will gather them, ﴿then let us invoke earnestly﴾ (nabtahil: we humble ourselves in supplication) ﴿and lay the curse of Allah upon the liars﴾ by saying: "O Allah, curse the liar concerning the affair of Jesus." The Prophet (ﷺ) invoked this against the delegation of Najran when they argued with him about it. They said: "Let us consider our affair, then we will come to you." Their men of judgment said: "You know his prophethood, and that no people have ever sought a prophet's curse without being destroyed. So make peace with the man and depart." They then came to the Messenger (ﷺ) after he had gone out, accompanied by al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Fatimah and Ali, and he said to them: "When I supplicate, say Amin." But they refused to engage in mutual cursing and made a settlement with him for the jizyah. Related by Abu Nu'aym.

And from Ibn Abbas, he said: "If those who were going to engage in mutual invocation (mubahalah) had gone out, they would have returned finding neither wealth nor family." And it is narrated: "If they had gone out, they would have been burned."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 62:

﴿Indeed, this﴾ that is mentioned ﴿is the true narrative﴾ the true report about which there is no doubt, ﴿and there is no god except Allah. And indeed, Allah is the Almighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 63:

﴿Then if they turn away﴾ from faith, ﴿indeed Allah is Knowing of the corrupters﴾, so He will recompense them. In it there is the placing of the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 64:

﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allah,"﴾ [the Jews and the Christians]. ﴿Equitable﴾ is a verbal noun (maṣdar) in the sense of "level" (mustawin), its matter being level. ﴿Between us and you﴾ is that ﴿we will not worship except Allah, and not associate anything with Him, and not take one another as lords instead of Allah﴾, as you [i.e., the Jews and Christians] have taken the rabbis and the monks [as lords]. ﴿But if they turn away﴾ from monotheism, ﴿then say﴾ to them, ﴿"Bear witness that we are Muslims"﴾, i.e., monotheists.

The Jalalayn revealed when the Jews said, "Abraham was a Jew, and we are upon his religion," and the Christians said likewise: ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you argue﴾ dispute ﴿about Abraham﴾ on your claim that he was upon your religion, ﴿when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him﴾ by a long time; and after their revelation, Judaism and Christianity came into being. ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ ﴿the falsity of your statement﴾

Ha (ها) is for drawing attention. "Antum" (أنتم) is the subject (mubtada'), and "ha'ula'" (هَؤُلاءِ) is in the vocative; the predicate is: "You have argued about what you have knowledge of," concerning the matter of Musa and Isa, and your claim that you follow their religion. "Then why do you argue about what you have no knowledge of," concerning the matter of Ibrahim? "And Allah knows" his matter, "and you do not know." He, the Exalted, said this to absolve Ibrahim.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 67:

﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a ḥanīf﴾ (inclining away from all the religions toward the upright religion), ﴿a Muslim﴾ (a monotheist), ﴿and he was not of those who associate partners with God﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 68:

﴿Indeed, the closest of people﴾ are most entitled ﴿to Abraham are those who followed him﴾ during his time ﴿and this Prophet﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ), because of his agreement with him in most of his sharia ﴿and those who believe﴾ of his community. They are the ones who should say, "We are upon his religion," not you. ﴿And Allah is the Guardian of the believers﴾, their Helper and Protector.

Revealed when the Jews invited Mu'adh, Hudhayfah and 'Ammar to their religion: ﴿A group of the People of the Book wish they could lead you astray, but they lead astray none except themselves﴾, because the sin of their misguiding others falls upon them, and the believers do not obey them in it. ﴿And they do not perceive﴾ this.

O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah, [i.e., in] the Qur'an which includes the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿while you witness﴾ [that it is] the truth, knowing that it is the truth.

O People of the Scripture, why do you mix up the truth with falsehood (تَخْلِطُونَ, "you mingle"), by distortion and forgery (بِالتَّحْرِيفِ والتَّزْوِير), and conceal the truth (أيْ نَعْت النَّبِيّ, "that is, the description of the Prophet") while you know (أنَّهُ الحَقّ, "that it is the truth")?

Qur'anic verse: ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you mix up the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know?﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 72:

﴿And a group among the People of the Book said﴾ — the Jews, to one another: ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿at the beginning of the day﴾, its first part, ﴿and disbelieve at its end﴾, in it, ﴿perhaps they will turn back﴾, i.e., the believers, ﴿from their religion﴾, saying: "These people have not turned back from it after entering into it, and they are people of knowledge — it is only because of their knowledge of its falsehood."

And they also said: "Do not believe [i.e., do not affirm/acknowledge as true] except for those who follow your religion." Allah said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, guidance is the guidance of Allah"﴾ — addressed to them, O Muhammad — which is Islam; and whatever opposes it is misguidance. The clause is a parenthetical interjection. ﴿That [an]⦅i.e., lest⦆ one be given the like of what you were given﴾ — that is, [it is said] that one be given the like of what you were given, of the Book, the wisdom and the virtues. "That" (an) is the object of "do not believe," and the one excepted from ("anyone") has been placed before the exception. The meaning is: "Do not acknowledge that anyone is given such things, except for those who follow your religion." ﴿Or⦆ [that] ﴿they will argue with you⦆ — i.e., the believers will overcome you ﴿before your Lord⦆ on the Day of Resurrection, because your religion is more correct. In another reading, it is read as ʾa-an, with the interrogative hamzah of rebuke, meaning: "Will you acknowledge that anyone be given the like of it?" ﴿Say, "Indeed, bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills."﴾ So from where do you have [the assurance] that no one is given the like of what you were given? ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing⦆ — abundant in bounty ﴿All-Knowing⦆ of whoever is worthy of it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah Al 'Imran, verse 75:

﴿Among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar (a large quantity of wealth), will return it to you﴾ meaning, with a great amount of wealth, ﴿will return it to you﴾ because of his trustworthiness, like ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, with whom a man deposited a thousand and two hundred ūqiyya (a unit of weight) of gold, and he returned it to him. ﴿And among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you﴾ because of his treachery, ﴿unless you keep standing over him﴾ meaning, unless you do not part from him. Whenever you part from him, he denies it, like Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, with whom a man from Quraysh deposited a dinar, and he denied it. ﴿That﴾ meaning, the failure to return, ﴿is because they say﴾ because of their saying, ﴿"There is no blame on us regarding the ummiyyin"﴾ meaning, the Arabs, ﴿blame (sabīl)﴾ meaning, sin, because they regard it as lawful to wrong those who oppose their religion, and they attribute this to Him, exalted is He, ﴿and they speak falsehood against Allah﴾ in attributing that to Him, ﴿while they know﴾ that they are liars.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 76:

﴿Yes [there is no blame upon them] in regard to the unlettered;⁠ rather﴾ ﴿whoever fulfills his covenant﴾ that which he covenanted, or the covenant of Allah with him, of returning trusts and other things, ﴿and fears [Allah]﴾ by abandoning sins and performing acts of obedience, ﴿then indeed Allah loves those who fear [Him]﴾. In it is the placing of the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun, i.e., He loves them, meaning He rewards them.

It was revealed concerning the Jews when they altered the description of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the covenant of Allah made with them in the Torah, and concerning one who swears falsely in a claim or in the sale of a commodity. ﴿Indeed, those who exchange﴾ (yastabdiluna), i.e., substitute ﴿the covenant of Allah﴾ made with them regarding belief in the Prophet and the fulfilment of the trust, ﴿and their oaths﴾, i.e., their swearing by Him, the Exalted, falsely, ﴿for a little price﴾ of this world, ﴿those will have no share﴾ (nasib) ﴿in the Hereafter. And Allah will not speak to them﴾ in anger, ﴿nor look at them﴾, i.e., have mercy upon them, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them﴾, i.e., cleanse them, ﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾, i.e., painful.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 78:

﴿And indeed among them﴾ i.e., among the People of the Book, ﴿is a group﴾ a party, such as Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, ﴿who distort their tongues with the Book﴾ i.e., they twist them, by reciting it, away from what was revealed to what they have altered of the description of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the like, ﴿so that you may think it﴾ i.e., the altered part, ﴿to be from the Book﴾ which Allah revealed, ﴿but it is not from the Book. And they say, "It is from Allah," but it is not from Allah. And they speak falsehood about Allah while they know﴾ that they are lying.

Revealed when the Christians of Najran said that Jesus had commanded them to take him as a lord, and when some of the Muslims asked to prostrate to him (ﷺ): ﴿It is not for a man that Allah should give him the Book and the judgment (al-hukm), meaning the understanding of the Shari'ah, and the prophethood, and then he should say to the people, "Be servants of mine instead of Allah"; rather, [he would say], "Be rabbaniyyin," meaning scholars who act upon their knowledge, attributed to the Lord (al-Rabb) with the addition of an alif and a nun for emphasis, ﴾ by what you have been teaching (ta'lamun) the Book, with the letters pronounced either lightly or with gemination, ﴿and by what you have been studying (tadrusun)﴾. That is, because of this, for its benefit is that you may act upon it.

﴿Nor would He command you﴾. The verb is read with a *ḍammah* (*raf'*), making it a resumptive sentence (*istiʾnāf*, a new independent clause), so the subject is Allah. It is read with a *fatḥah* (*naṣb*) as a coordinated clause (*ʿaṭf*) following "yaqūl" (it is not for him to say), so the subject is a human being (al-bashar). ﴿that you take the angels and the prophets as lords﴾, as the Ṣābiʾah (Sabians) took the angels, the Jews took ʿUzayr, and the Christians took ʿĪsā. ﴿Would He command you to disbelief after you have submitted?﴾ It is not befitting for Him to do this.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 81:

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿when﴾ (idh) [the time when] ﴿Allah took the covenant of the Prophets﴾, their pledge, ﴿that﴾ (lamā), with a fatha on the lām, it is for the beginning of the sentence and for emphasizing the sense of oath contained in the taking of the covenant; with a kasra on the lām, it is connected to "took" (akhadha), and mā is a relative pronoun in both readings, meaning "that which" ﴿I have given you﴾ of it, and in another reading "We have given you" ﴿of Book and wisdom; then there has come to you a Messenger confirming what is with you﴾ of the Book and wisdom, and he is Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿you shall believe in him and you shall help him﴾. This is the answer to the oath, if you reach him; and their communities follow them in that. ﴿He said﴾, may He be exalted, to them: ﴿Do you affirm﴾ this ﴿and accept﴾, i.e. you accept, ﴿on that My burden﴾, i.e. My covenant? ﴿They said: We affirm.﴾ He said: ﴿Then bear witness﴾ against yourselves and your followers to that ﴿and I am with you among the witnesses﴾ against you and against them.
﴿Whoever turns away after that﴾ refuses, ﴿after that﴾ covenant, ﴿those are the defiantly disobedient﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 83:

﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah?﴾ With the ya' and the ta' (i.e., "yabghūn" and "tabghūn"), meaning: those who turn away. ﴿And to Him has submitted﴾ surrendered/yielded ﴿whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly﴾ without refusal ﴿and unwillingly﴾ upon witnessing that which compels them to it. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ with the ta' and the ya'; and the hamzah at the beginning of the verse is for denunciation (istinkār).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 84:

﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad: ﴿We believe in God, and in what has been revealed to us, and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes﴾ — their descendants — ﴿and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the Prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them﴾ by affirming or denying any of them, ﴿and to Him we are Muslims﴾ sincere in worship. It was revealed concerning those who apostatized and joined the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 85:

﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.﴾ (He will be) for his destiny to the everlasting Fire upon him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 86:

﴿How﴾, i.e., it is not (the case that) ﴿Allah guides a people who disbelieve after their belief and who testify﴾, i.e., their testimony, ﴿that the Messenger is true﴾, and ﴿the clear proofs had come to them﴾, the evident arguments for the truthfulness of the Prophet. ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, i.e., the disbelievers.

﴿Abiding therein﴾, i.e., the curse or the Fire, the one indicated by it (by the pronoun "therein"). ﴿Their punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved﴾, meaning they will not be given respite.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 89:

﴿Except for those who repent after that and make amends﴾ their deeds, ﴿for indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ to them ﴿and Merciful﴾ toward them.

It was revealed concerning the Jews: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾ in Jesus ﴿after their belief﴾ in Moses ﴿then increase in disbelief﴾ in Muhammad ﴿their repentance will never be accepted﴾ if they are in the throes of death (ghargharu) or die as disbelievers ﴿and those are the astray﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 91:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold﴾ — the amount that would fill it — ﴿even if he were to ransom himself with it.﴾ He placed the fa' (the particle "then") in the predicate of inna (indeed) because of the resemblance of "those who" to a conditional clause, and to indicate that the non-acceptance is caused by dying upon disbelief. ﴿Those — for them is a painful punishment﴾ — painful, causing pain. ﴿And they will have no helpers﴾ — preventers from it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 92:

﴿You will never attain righteousness﴾, i.e., its reward, which is Paradise, ﴿until you spend﴾, i.e., give in charity, ﴿of that which you love﴾ from your wealth. ﴿And whatever you spend, indeed Allah knows it﴾, so He will reward you for it.

It was revealed when the Jews said, "You claim that you follow the religion of Abraham," and he (ﷺ) would not eat camel meat or drink its milk. ﴿All food was lawful﴾, permissible, ﴿for the Children of Israel, except what Israel had forbidden﴾, namely Ya'qub (Jacob), ﴿upon himself﴾. That was camel meat, for he had contracted '*irq al-nasa* (sciatica), with the *fatha* and a shortened vowel. He vowed that if he was cured he would not eat it, so it was forbidden to him ﴿before the Tawrah (Torah) was revealed﴾. That was after Abraham, and it was not forbidden in Abraham's time, as they claimed. ﴿Say﴾ to them, ﴿Then bring the Tawrah and recite it﴾, so that the truth of your claim becomes clear, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in it. So they were confounded and did not bring it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 94:

﴿Then whoever fabricates a lie against Allah after this﴾ i.e., after the proof has become manifest that the prohibition originated from Ya'qub (Jacob), and not in the time of Ibrahim (Abraham). ﴿Those are the wrongdoers﴾ those who transgress from the truth to falsehood.

﴿Say: "Allah has spoken the truth"﴾ in this, as in everything He has informed of, ﴿so follow the religion of Ibrahim﴾ which I follow, ﴿as a ḥanīf﴾ inclining away from every religion to Islam, ﴿and he was not of the polytheists﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 96:

It was revealed when they said: "Our qibla (direction of prayer) is before your qibla." ﴿Indeed, the first House established﴾ for worship, ﴿for mankind﴾ on earth, ﴿is that at Bakkah﴾ (with the letter bā' in dialect, for Makkah). It was named so because it crushes (tabukk) the necks of tyrants, i.e., breaks them. It was built by the angels before the creation of Adam, and al-Aqsa was built after it, and between them was forty years, as in the hadith of the two Sahihs. And in a hadith: "It was the first thing to appear on the surface of the water when the heavens and the earth were created, a white foam, and the earth was spread out from beneath it." ﴿Blessed﴾, a state (ḥāl) of "that," i.e., possessing blessing. ﴿And a guidance for the worlds﴾, because it is their qibla.

﴿In it are clear signs﴾, among them ﴿the Station of Ibrahim (Maqam Ibrahim)﴾, that is, the stone on which he stood while the House was being built. His footprints remained in it, and it has lasted to this day despite the passage of time and the many hands that have touched it. Among the signs is also the multiplication of good deeds performed in it, and that birds do not fly over it. ﴿Whoever enters it is secure﴾, meaning he is not to be harmed by killing, wrongdoing, or anything else. ﴿Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to God by the people﴾, where wājib (واجِب, obligatory) is the predicate. The vowel of the ḥāʾ in ḥijj (حِجّ) may be read with a kasra or a fatḥa; these are two dialects for the verbal noun of ḥajja, meaning "to intend." The phrase may be substituted (badal) for "the people" (an-nās). ﴿For whoever is able to make his way to it﴾, that is, has a path. He (ﷺ) explained this as provision and a mount; narrated by al-Ḥākim and others. ﴿And whoever disbelieves﴾, in God or in what He has made obligatory of the pilgrimage, ﴿then God is Self-sufficient, independent of all the worlds﴾, of humankind, the jinn and the angels, and of their worship.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 98:

﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah, while Allah is Witness over what you do?"﴾ [The verses of Allah:] the Qur'an. [Allah is Witness over what you do:] so He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 99:

﴿Say: "O People of the Scripture, why do you avert﴾ turn away ﴿from the way of Allah﴾ i.e., His religion ﴿those who have believed,﴾ by your denying the Prophet and concealing His blessing, ﴿seeking to make it crooked﴾ i.e., you seek the way to be ﴿crooked,﴾ 'iwajan being a verbal noun in the sense of mu'wajjah, i.e., deviating ﴿from the truth,﴾ ﴿while you are witnesses?﴾ knowing that the religion approved and upright is the religion of Islam, as it is in your Scripture. ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾ of disbelief and denial, and He only delays you until your appointed time in order to requite you."﴾

It was revealed when some Jews passed by the Aws and the Khazraj and their closeness to one another angered them. So they reminded them of what had existed between them in the Jahiliyya (the Age of Ignorance) of strife, and they quarrelled and nearly fought one another. ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you, after your belief, to disbelievers.﴾

﴿And how can you disbelieve﴾ is an interrogative (istifham) of amazement and rebuke, ﴿while the verses of Allah are recited to you, and among you is His Messenger? And whoever holds fast﴾ clings ﴿to Allah, then he has been guided to a straight path﴾.

O you who believe, ﴿fear God as He should be feared﴾, by being obeyed and not disobeyed, thanked and not ungrateful, and remembered and not forgotten. They said, "O Messenger of God, who is able to do this?" So it was abrogated (naskh) by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So fear God as much as you are able﴾ and ﴿do not die except as Muslims﴾, that is, monotheists.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 103:

﴿And hold fast, all together, to the rope of Allah﴾ — i.e., His religion — ﴿and do not become divided﴾ after Islam. ﴿And remember the blessing of Allah upon you﴾ — His favour — ﴿when you were enemies [of one another] before Islam, so He brought together your hearts﴾ — He joined them — ﴿by Islam, and you became, by His blessing, brothers﴾ in religion and in mutual allegiance. ﴿And you were on the brink of a pit of Fire﴾ — on its edge — ﴿and He saved you from it﴾ through faith. ﴿Thus﴾ — as He has made clear to you what has been mentioned — ﴿Allah makes clear to you His verses that you may be guided﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 104:

﴿And let there be from you a community who invite to the good﴾ — i.e., Islam — ﴿and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.﴾ ﴿And those are they﴾ — the ones who invite, enjoin and forbid — ﴿they are the successful﴾ — the victorious. The particle "min" (from/some of) is for partitive (tab'id) meaning, because what is mentioned is a communal obligation (fard kifayah, a duty which, if fulfilled by some, lifts it from the rest), which does not bind every member of the community, nor is it fitting for every individual, such as the ignorant person.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 105:

﴿And do not be like those who became divided [from their religion] and differed [concerning it] after the clear proofs had come to them.﴾ They are the Jews and the Christians. ﴿For them there is a great punishment.﴾

﴿On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection. ﴿As for those whose faces turned black﴾, and they are the disbelievers, they will be cast into the Fire, and it will be said to them as a rebuke: ﴿Did you disbelieve after your belief?﴾ referring to the Day of the taking of the *mithaq* (covenant).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 107:

﴿And as for those whose faces will turn white﴾, they are the believers, ﴿they will be in the mercy of Allah﴾, i.e., His Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 108:

﴿Those﴾ i.e., these verses ﴿are the verses of Allah, which We recite to you﴾ O Muhammad ﴿in truth. And Allah does not desire injustice for the worlds﴾ by seizing them without a crime.
﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ in ownership, creation and servitude, ﴿and to Allah it returns﴾, i.e., it becomes (taṣīr).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 110:

﴿You (are)﴾ O community of Muhammad, in the knowledge of God, Exalted is He, ﴿the best community brought forth﴾ made manifest ﴿for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and believing in God. And if the People of the Book had believed, it would have been ﴿better for them. Among them are believers﴾ such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, may God be pleased with him, and his companions, ﴿but most of them are defiant transgressors﴾ disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 111:

﴿They will not harm you﴾ meaning: the Jews, O assembly of Muslims, ﴿except for some harm﴾ by the tongue, through abuse and threats. ﴿And if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you﴾ routed, ﴿then they will not be helped﴾ against you; rather, victory will be yours over them.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 3, verse 112:

﴿They were struck with humiliation wherever they were found﴾, i.e., wherever they were encountered, so there is no might for them and no protection, ﴿except﴾ when they are ﴿under a covenant from God and a covenant from the people﴾, the believers. This is their covenant with them, a guarantee of safety in exchange for paying the jizyah (poll tax). That is, there is no protection for them other than this. ﴿They have returned﴾, i.e., they came back, ﴿with wrath from God, and they were struck with wretchedness.﴾ That is because ﴿they used to disbelieve in the signs of God and kill the prophets without right.﴾ That is because ﴿they disobeyed﴾ God's command ﴿and used to transgress﴾, going beyond the lawful to the unlawful.

﴿They are not all alike﴾, i.e. the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) ﴿are not equal﴾, being unequal ﴿among the People of the Book is an upright community﴾, meaning steadfast and firm upon the truth, like ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam (may Allah be pleased with him) and his companions. ﴿They recite the signs of Allah during the hours of the night﴾, i.e. during its periods, ﴿while they prostrate﴾, meaning they pray, as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 114:

﴿They believe in Allah and the Last Day, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and hasten to do good deeds. And those﴾ are the ones described by what Allah has mentioned ﴿among the righteous﴾. And among them are those who are not like that, and they are not among the righteous.

﴿And whatever good you do﴾ with *بِالتّاءِ* (with the ta', addressing you, O community) and with *والياء* (with the ya', meaning the upright community), ﴿you will never be denied it﴾ in both readings, meaning you will not lose its reward; rather, you will be recompensed for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 116:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against Allah﴾ (lan tughniya: will avail, i.e., will repel) ﴿anything from Him﴾, i.e., from His punishment. He singled out these two for mention because a person repels [harm] from himself sometimes by ransoming with wealth, and sometimes by seeking help from his children.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 117:

﴿Parable﴾ is an attribute of ﴿what they spend﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿in this worldly life﴾, in their enmity to the Prophet, by way of charity and the like, ﴿is like a wind in which is a cold﴾, i.e., intense heat or intense cold, ﴿that has struck the tilth﴾, i.e., the crop, ﴿of a people who have wronged themselves﴾ by disbelief and disobedience, ﴿and destroyed it﴾, so that they do not benefit from it. Likewise, their expenditures are lost, and they do not benefit from them. ﴿And Allah did not wrong them﴾ by the loss of their expenditures, ﴿but they wronged themselves﴾ by disbelief, which necessitates their loss.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 118:

﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimate friends (biṭāna) those other than your own [kind]﴾, who would reveal your secrets, ﴿from among other than yourselves﴾, i.e., other than you, from among the Jews, the Christians and the hypocrites. ﴿They spare no effort to corrupt you﴾: this is in the accusative by the removal of the preposition, i.e., they do not fall short in causing you corruption. ﴿They wish﴾, i.e., they desire ﴿what distresses you﴾, i.e., your distress (ʿanatakum), which is severe harm. ﴿Hatred has already appeared﴾, i.e., become evident, ﴿from their mouths﴾, through slandering you and disclosing your secrets to the polytheists. ﴿What their breasts conceal is greater﴾ of enmity. ﴿We have already made the signs clear to you﴾ regarding their enmity, ﴿if you use your reason﴾ [in this matter], so do not take them as allies.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti), on Surah 3, verse 119:

﴿Ha﴾ is for alerting (attention): ﴿you﴾ O ﴿these﴾ believers, ﴿you love them﴾ because of their kinship to you and their friendship, ﴿but they do not love you﴾ because of their opposition to you in religion, ﴿and you believe in the Book, all of it﴾ i.e., in all the books, ﴿while they do not believe in your Book.﴾ ﴿And when they meet you, they say, "We believe," but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage﴾ the tips of the fingers, ﴿out of rage﴾ intense anger at what they see of your harmony. The biting of the fingertips is used figuratively to express intense anger, even though there is no actual biting. ﴿Say: "Die in your rage!"﴾ i.e., remain in it until death, ﴿for you will never see anything that pleases you.﴾ ﴿Indeed Allah knows well what is in the breasts﴾ what is in the hearts, including what these people conceal.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 120:

﴿If good touches you﴾ befalls you, ﴿a good﴾ a blessing, such as victory and booty, ﴿it grieves them﴾ distresses them, ﴿and if an evil befalls you﴾ such as defeat and drought, ﴿they rejoice at it﴾. The conditional clause is linked to the preceding conditional clause, and what lies between them is a parenthetical statement. The meaning is that they are extremely hostile toward you, so why do you take them as allies? Therefore, shun them. ﴿But if you are patient﴾ in the face of their harm, ﴿and are mindful of Allah﴾ regarding your alliance with them and other matters, ﴿their plot will not harm you at all﴾ — the word "yadurrukum" may be read with a kasra on the dad, with a sukun on the ra, with a damma on the ra, and with a shadda on the ra (ḍarr / yaḍurrukum variants). ﴿Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾ — "ya'malūn" may be read with the yā' or the tā'. He is Knowing, so He will recompense them for it.

The Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 3, verse 121:

﴿And﴾ mention, O Muhammad, ﴿when you set out early in the morning from your family﴾ from Madinah, ﴿to settle the believers in positions﴾ you cause them to descend to, ﴿for battle. And Allah is Hearing﴾ of your words, ﴿Knowing﴾ of your conditions. This was the Day of Uhud. The Prophet (ﷺ) went out with a thousand men, or with fifty fewer than a thousand, while the polytheists numbered three thousand. He descended at al-Shi'b on Saturday, the seventh of Shawwal, in the third year after the Hijrah, and he placed his back and his army toward Uhud. He arranged their rows and seated a company of archers, appointing over them ʿAbd Allah ibn Jubayr at the foot of the mountain, and he said: "Shower them on our behalf with arrows, so that they do not come at us from behind us, and do not leave your position. Whether we are defeated or we are victorious."

Verse 122 (Tafsir al-Jalalayn):

﴿When⦆ is a substitute (badal) for the earlier ﴿when﴾, ﴿two groups of you, the Banu Salamah and the Banu Harithah, the two wings of the army, were about to lose heart (hammat)﴾: ﴿that they should falter﴾, i.e., turn coward in the fighting and withdraw, when ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, the hypocrite (munafiq), returned with his companions and said: "Why should we kill ourselves and our children?" He also said to Abu Jabir al-Sulami, who had said to him, "I adjure you by Allah regarding your Prophet and yourselves; if we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you," [so] Allah steadied them and they did not turn back. ﴿But Allah is their protector﴾, their helper, ﴿and in Allah let the believers put their trust﴾, that is, let them place their reliance in Him alone and none other.

It was revealed when they were defeated, as a reminder to them of God's blessing: ﴿And God had already helped you at Badr﴾, a place between Mecca and Medina, ﴿when you were weak﴾, through having few in number and few weapons. ﴿So be mindful of God, that perhaps you may be grateful﴾ for His blessings.

﴿Idh﴾ (إذْ) is an adverb of time (ẓarf) governing "your victory" (li-naṣrikum). ﴿When you were saying to the believers﴾ ﴿taqūl lil-mu'minīn﴾, promising them to reassure them (tu'idu-hum taṭmīnan). ﴿Will it not suffice you that your Lord should aid you﴾ ﴿yumiddakum﴾, meaning help you (yu'īnukum), ﴿with three thousand angels sent down﴾ ﴿munzalīn﴾, read with the light (takhfīf) and the doubled (tashdīd) forms.

Yes. That will suffice you. (And in Surat al-Anfal it is with a thousand, because He first supplied them with that number, then it became three thousand, then five thousand, as the Exalted said: ﴿If you are patient﴾ in facing the enemy ﴿and fear Allah﴾ by not opposing Him ﴿and they come upon you﴾, that is the polytheists, ﴿immediately﴾, at that moment, ﴿your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, marked﴾ — with the waw read with a kasra or a fatha — meaning distinguished by their marks. And they were patient, and Allah fulfilled His promise by the angels fighting alongside them, on piebald horses, wearing yellow or white turbans, letting them hang down between their shoulders.)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 126:

﴿And Allah did not make it⦅i.e., the reinforcement⦆ except as good news for you⦅of victory⦆﴾ and that your hearts may be assured thereby⦅and so not be dismayed at the great number of the enemy and your own small number⦆. ﴿And victory is not except from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ He gives it to whom He wills, and it is not by the multitude of troops.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 127:

﴿Liyaqta'a﴾ (so that He might cut off) is connected to "nasarakum" (helped you), i.e., ﴿liyuhlika ṭarafan min alladhīna kafarū﴾ (that He might destroy a portion of those who disbelieved) by killing and capture; ﴿aw yakbitahum﴾ (or subdue them) yudhillahum (humiliate them) by defeat; ﴿fa-yanqalibū﴾ (so that they return) yarji'ū (go back) ﴿khā'ibīna﴾ (frustrated), having not attained what they had aimed at.

It was revealed when his (ﷺ) lower incisor (rubā'iyyah) was broken and his face was wounded on the day of Uhud, and he said: "How will a people prosper who stain the face of their Prophet with blood?" ﴿You have no say in the matter﴾; rather the matter belongs to God, so be patient. ﴿Or﴾ in the sense of "until" ﴿He turns to them (in mercy)﴾ by means of Islam, ﴿or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers﴾ through disbelief.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 129:

﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, in dominion, creation and servitude. ﴿He forgives whom He wills﴾, forgiveness for him, ﴿and punishes whom He wills﴾, punishment for him. ﴿And Allah is Most Forgiving﴾ to His allies, ﴿Most Merciful﴾ to the people of His obedience.

O you who believe, do not consume usury (ribā) doubled and redoubled (ṭʿafan muḍāʿafatan), (meaning) with a thousand and less than that, by increasing the money when the term falls due and postponing the demand [for payment]. ﴿And fear God﴾ by abandoning it, ﴿so that you may be successful﴾, that is, that you may win.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 3, verse 131:

﴿And guard yourselves against the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾ — that you be punished by it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 133:

﴿And hasten﴾ with a waw and without it (wa-sari'u / sari'u) ﴿to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth, whose breadth is the heavens and the earth﴾ i.e., like their breadth were one of them joined to the other; and al-ʿarḍ (the breadth) means the expanse. ﴿It has been prepared for the God-fearing (al-muttaqin)﴾ by performing acts of obedience and abandoning acts of disobedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 134:

﴿Those who spend﴾ in obedience to God, ﴿in ease and in hardship﴾ — in prosperity and in adversity; ﴿and those who restrain their anger﴾ — who refrain from carrying it out although they are able to; ﴿and who pardon people﴾ — those who have wronged them, meaning those who abandon punishing them; ﴿and God loves the good-doers﴾ — by these deeds, meaning He rewards them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 135:

﴿And those who, when they commit an indecency﴾ a grave sin, such as fornication, ﴿or wrong themselves﴾ with something less than that, such as kissing, ﴿remember Allah﴾ i.e., His threat, ﴿and seek forgiveness for their sins﴾ — and who ﴿forgives sins but Allah?﴾ i.e., none ﴿and do not persist in what they have done﴾ i.e., do not keep doing it, but desist from it, ﴿while they know﴾ that what they committed is an act of disobedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 136:

﴿Those, their reward is forgiveness from their Lord, and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾ [khalidin] is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl muqaddarah), meaning: intending to abide therein forever when they enter them. ﴿And excellent is the reward of the workers﴾ [i.e., of those who work] by obedience (al-ṭāʿah); this is the reward.

It was revealed concerning the defeat at Uhud: **"Ways (sunan) have passed before you"** — tariq (ways, manners of conduct) — **among the disbelievers, by My granting them respite, then I seized them.** **"So travel in the earth"** — O believers — **"and see how was the end of those who denied"** — the messengers; that is, the final outcome of them, [which was] destruction. So do not grieve over their victory, for I grant them respite until their appointed time.
This is the Qur'an, a clarification for mankind, all of them, and a guidance from misguidance, and an admonition for the God-fearing among them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 139:

﴿Do not weaken﴾ (lit. do not become feeble) in fighting the disbelievers, ﴿nor grieve﴾ over what befell you at Uhud, ﴿for you will have the upper hand﴾ with victory over them, ﴿if you are [true] believers﴾ in truth. Its response (jawab, the answer to the conditional clause) is indicated by the whole of what precedes it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 140:

﴿If a wound touches you﴾ it afflicts you at Uhud, ﴿a wound﴾ (qarh, with the qaf either fatha or damma), meaning distress from a wound or the like, ﴿then the people﴾ the disbelievers ﴿have been touched by a wound like it﴾ at Badr. ﴿And We alternate these days﴾ We turn them ﴿among the people﴾, one day for one group and another day for another, ﴿so that they may take heed﴾; ﴿and that Allah may know﴾ with knowledge of manifestation, ﴿those who believe﴾, those who were sincere in their faith apart from others, ﴿and take martyrs from among you﴾, honouring them with martyrdom; ﴿and Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾, the disbelievers, meaning He will punish them, and what He bestows upon them is a gradual lure (istidraj).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 141:

﴿And that Allah may purify those who believe﴾ He purifies them from sins through what befalls them, ﴿and destroy the disbelievers﴾ He destroys them.

Or did you think you would enter Paradise without Allah first knowing those of you who strive, and knowing the steadfast? (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, on 3:142)

Wait, that is not what the passage says. Here is the faithful translation:

"Or" (bal, meaning "rather"): "did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah had not yet known those of you who strove, and [had not known] the steadfast"; the words "and had not yet" (wa-lamma) and "and had not" (wa-lam) mark the negation.

Correction, to give the text exactly as it stands:

Or (bal, "rather"): "Did you think that you would enter Paradise, while Allah has not yet known those of you who strive?" ﴿Or did you think you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those of you who strive, and the steadfast?﴾

Here is the translation in full, as it should appear:

"Rather, did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah had not [yet] known those of you who strove (jahadu), by way of manifest knowledge (ilm zuhur), and [had not known] the steadfast (al-sabirin) in times of hardship?"

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 143:

﴿And you had certainly wished for death before you encountered it﴾. Here there is an elision of one of the two tā's in the original (tatamannawna, becoming tamannawna): ﴿death before you encountered it﴾, when you said, "Would that we had a day like the day of Badr, so that we might attain what its martyrs attained." ﴿Then you have certainly seen it﴾, i.e., its cause, which is war, ﴿while you were looking on﴾, i.e., with open eyes, contemplating the state of affairs as it is. So why did you flee?

It was revealed concerning their rout when it was circulated that the Prophet (ﷺ) had been killed, and the hypocrites said to them, "If he has been killed, then return to your religion."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 144:

﴿Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed,﴾ like others, ﴿will you turn back on your heels?﴾ That is, will you return to disbelief?
