The final clause is the place of the rhetorical interrogative of denial, meaning: he was not worshipped, so do not turn back. ﴿And whoever turns back on his heels, he will not harm Allah at all,﴾ but he only harms himself. ﴿And Allah will reward the grateful﴾ for His favours, by steadfastness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 145:

﴿And no soul can die except by the permission of Allah﴾ by His decree ﴿a decree with a fixed term﴾: "kitāban" is a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning Allah has decreed that ﴿with a fixed term﴾, appointed and timed, neither advancing nor delaying. So why did you flee! Flight does not avert death, and steadfastness does not cut short life. ﴿And whoever desires﴾ by his deed ﴿the reward of this world﴾, meaning its recompense from it, ﴿We give him from it﴾ what has been allotted to him, and he has no share in the Hereafter. ﴿And whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We give him from it﴾, meaning from its reward.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 3, verse 146:

﴿And how many a prophet﴾ how many (kam) ﴿has been killed﴾ and in another reading, ﴿fought﴾ (qatala), with its subject being the pronoun in it, ﴿with him﴾ is the predicate of a subject which is ﴿multitudes of God-fearing men (ribbiyyun) in great number﴾ large groups. ﴿Yet they did not weaken﴾ they did not lose heart ﴿for what befell them in the way of God﴾ of wounds and the killing of their prophets and companions, ﴿nor did they become feeble﴾ in jihad, ﴿nor did they submit﴾ they did not yield to their enemy, as you did when it was said that the Prophet had been killed. ﴿And God loves those who are steadfast﴾ in the face of trials, meaning He will reward them.

﴿And their words﴾ at the killing of their Prophet, despite their steadfastness and patience, ﴿were only that they said: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses﴾ (i.e., our going beyond the limit) ﴿in our affair﴾, indicating that what befell them was due to the wrongness of their own actions, and as a humbling of themselves, ﴿and make our feet firm﴾ with strength in jihad."
﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world﴾: victory and booty. ﴿and the good reward of the Hereafter﴾, namely Paradise. Its goodness lies in His bounty exceeding what they deserved.
﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve﴾ in what they command you ﴿they will return you﴾ to disbelief.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 150:

﴿Nay, God is your Protector (mawlakum)﴾, i.e., your Helper, ﴿and He is the best of helpers﴾. So obey Him, not them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 151:

﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾ (al-ru'b, read with a sukun or a damma on the ʿayn), meaning fear. They had resolved, after their departure from Uhud, to return and wipe out the Muslims, but they were struck with fear and did not return. ﴿Because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority﴾, that is, because of their associating others with Allah, which lacked any proof (ḥujja) for His worship, namely the idols. ﴿Their abode is the Fire, and wretched is the dwelling of the wrongdoers﴾, meaning the place of residence (mathwā) of the disbelievers, is the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 152:

﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you﴾ [of victory] to you, ﴿when you were killing them by His permission﴾ killing them, by His will, ﴿until, when you lost courage﴾ became cowardly about fighting, and the response of "when" is indicated by what precedes it, i.e., He withheld His victory from you, ﴿and disputed concerning the matter﴾ differed, ﴿about the matter﴾ i.e., the command of the Prophet ﷺ to remain at the foot of the mountain for shooting. Some of you said: "Let us go, for our companions have been victorious," and some of you said: "We will not disobey the command of the Prophet ﷺ." ﴿And you disobeyed﴾ his command, and so you abandoned the position in pursuit of the spoils, ﴿after He had shown you﴾ Allah ﴿what you love﴾ of victory ﴿among you are those who desire this world﴾ who abandoned the position for the spoils, ﴿and among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾ who stood firm with it until they were killed, like ʿAbd Allah ibn Jubayr and his companions. ﴿Then He turned you away from them﴾ a conjunction with the presumed response of "when": He turned you back to defeat, ﴿from them﴾ i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿that He might test you﴾ that He might examine you, so that the sincere might be distinguished from others. ﴿And certainly He has pardoned you﴾ for what you committed. ﴿And Allah is bountiful to the believers﴾ through pardon.

When you were fleeing up the slope, not turning back for anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind you (i.e., from your rear), saying: "O servants of God, come back to me!" (﴿إذْ تُصْعِدُونَ﴾ "when you were ascending" — i.e., going far off into the land, fleeing; ﴿ولا تَلْوُونَ﴾ "and you did not turn back" — i.e., you did not climb/look back ﴿عَلى أحَد﴾ "for anyone"; ﴿والرَّسُول يَدْعُوكُمْ فِي أُخْراكُمْ﴾ "while the Messenger was calling you in your rear" — i.e., from behind you).

﴿فَأَثابَكُمْ﴾ "So He rewarded you" — i.e., He repaid you ﴿غَمًّا﴾ "with grief" through the defeat ﴿بِغَمٍّ﴾ "with grief" — because of the grief you caused the Messenger by disobeying him. It has also been said that the preposition (bi) here carries the meaning of (ʿalā, "upon"), i.e., a grief multiplied upon the grief of losing the spoils of war.

﴿لِكَيْلا﴾ "so that not" — this is connected to (ʿafā, "He pardoned"), or to (athābakum, "He rewarded you"), in which case the (lā) is extra. ﴿تَحْزَنُوا عَلى ما فاتَكُمْ﴾ "you would grieve over what had escaped you" — i.e., of the spoils of war ﴿ولا ما أصابَكُمْ﴾ "nor over what had befallen you" — i.e., of killing and defeat.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 154:

﴿Then He sent down upon you, after the distress, security﴾ (amnan) ﴿—drowsiness﴾ (nu'asan), replacing ﴿overcomes﴾ (yaghshā), with the ya' and the ta' (both readings) ﴿—a group of you﴾, who were the believers, so they swayed under the shields (al-hujaf), and swords kept falling from their hands ﴿—and another group, who were concerned only for themselves﴾, meaning, they were moved by worry, so their only desire was to save themselves, apart from the Prophet and his companions, so they did not sleep; these were the hypocrites ﴿—thinking about Allah﴾ (zannan) ﴿other than the truth, the thought﴾, meaning, like ﴿the thought of the Jahiliyyah﴾ (the Age of Ignorance), in that they believed that the Prophet had been killed or would not be helped ﴿—they say: "Is there﴾ (hal) ﴿any﴾ (ma) ﴿for us in the matter﴾, meaning, the victory that we were promised, ﴿anything?"﴾ Say ﴿to them﴾: ﴿"Indeed the matter, all of it﴾ (with the accusative as an emphasis, and with the nominative as a subject and predicate) ﴿belongs to Allah"﴾, meaning, the decree belongs to Him; He does what He wills. ﴿They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal﴾ (yudhhirūn) ﴿to you. They say﴾ (this is an explanation of what precedes): ﴿"Had there been anything for us in the matter, we would not have been killed here"﴾, meaning, had the choice been ours, we would not have gone out and so would not have been killed; but we were brought out against our will. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"Even if you had been in your houses﴾, and among you were those whom Allah had decreed to be slain, ﴿those decreed to be slain would have gone out﴾ (kharaja), ﴿to their places of death﴾ (maḍāji'ihim), meaning, their places of falling, and they would have been killed; their sitting at home would not have saved them, because the decree of Him, exalted is He, is certain without doubt. ﴿And﴾ He did what He did at Uhud ﴿so that Allah might test﴾ (yabtaliya), meaning, He might examine ﴿what is in your breasts﴾, meaning, your hearts, of sincerity and hypocrisy, ﴿and so that He might purify﴾ (yumahhiṣa), meaning, distinguish ﴿what is in your hearts. And Allah is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning, of what is in the hearts; nothing is hidden from Him. He tests only in order to make it manifest to the people.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 155:

﴿Indeed, those of you who turned away﴾ from the fighting, ﴿on the day the two hosts met﴾ the host of the Muslims and the host of the disbelievers at Uhud, and they were Muslims, except twelve men, ﴿it was only that Satan caused them to slip﴾ made them slip, ﴿through some of what they had earned﴾ of sins, namely their opposition to the command of the Prophet, ﴿and Allah has already pardoned them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ toward the believers, ﴿Forbearing﴾ and does not hasten to punish the disobedient.

O you who believe, do not be like those who disbelieve, meaning the hypocrites, ﴿and say to their brethren﴾, meaning concerning them, ﴿when they travel through the land﴾, meaning journey, ﴿and die,﴾ ﴿or were fighting (ghuzzan)﴾, the plural of ghazin (a warrior), ﴿and were killed,﴾ ﴿"Had they remained with us, they would not have died, nor would they have been killed."﴾ That is, do not say as they say. ﴿So that Allah may make that (saying) a regret in their hearts.﴾ That is, the saying will bring about in the end regret for them. ﴿And Allah gives life and causes death.﴾ So sitting at home does not prevent death. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ Read with the ta' and with the ya' (i.e., "what you do" or "what they do"). ﴿He is Seeing,﴾ so He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 157:

﴿And if you are killed in the way of Allah﴾ — the lam here is the lam of oath (lam al-qasam) — ﴿or you die﴾ — read with a damma and a kasra on the mim, from māta yamūtu, meaning death came to you in it (i.e., in the jihad) — ﴿surely forgiveness from Allah﴾ (maghfira kā'ina) ﴿for your sins and mercy from Him for you upon that﴾ — the lam and what follows it are the answer to the oath, and it is in the position of the verb, a mubtada' (inchoative) whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿better than what they gather﴾ of the worldly goods, read with the ta' and the ya'.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 158:

﴿Wa-la-in﴾ the lam is an oath particle. ﴿Mut-um﴾ (you die) in either of the two ways, ﴿aw qutiltum﴾ (or you are killed) in jihad or otherwise, ﴿la-ila Allah﴾ (surely to God), not to anything else, ﴿tuhsharun﴾ (you will be gathered) in the Hereafter, whereupon He will recompense you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 159:

﴿So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿i.e., you made your character easy toward them when they opposed you﴾. ﴿And had you been harsh﴾, bad-tempered, ﴿hard-hearted﴾, rough, ﴿and so you were severe with them﴾, ﴿they would have dispersed from around you﴾, ﴿scattered﴾. ﴿So pardon them﴾, overlook ﴿what they committed﴾, ﴿and ask forgiveness for them﴾ for their sins, ﴿until I forgive them﴾. ﴿And consult them in the matter﴾, i.e., extract their opinions ﴿concerning your affair﴾ of war and other things, to soothe their hearts and so that you may set a precedent through them. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to consult them very often. ﴿So when you have decided﴾ upon carrying out what you intend after consultation, ﴿then rely upon Allah﴾, trust in Him and not in the consultation. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 160:

﴿If Allah helps you﴾ He will aid you against your enemy, as on the Day of Badr, ﴿none can overcome you. But if He forsakes you﴾ He withholds His help from you, as on the Day of Uhud, ﴿who is there that can help you after Him?﴾ i.e., after His forsaking you, meaning there is no helper for you. ﴿And upon Allah﴾ alone, not another, ﴿let the believers put their trust﴾ let them rely (lit. let them be confident).

Revealed when a red cloak (qatifa hamra') was missing on the day of Uhud, and some people said: "Perhaps the Prophet took it." ﴿It is not for a prophet﴾ it is not fitting for him ﴿to commit fraud (ghull)﴾ to betray in the distribution of the spoils. So do not suppose that of him. In another recitation, it is read in the passive voice (bi'l-bina' li'l-maf'ul): that he be attributed to fraud. ﴿And whoever commits fraud will come on the Day of Resurrection bearing what he defrauded﴾ carrying it upon his neck. ﴿Then every soul will be paid in full (tuwaffa) for what it earned (kasabat)﴾ what it did, ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾ in anything, ﴾, [the fraudster and others alike] as recompense.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 162:

﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah﴾ and obeys Him and does not embezzle ﴿like one who returns﴾ who goes back ﴿with wrath from Allah﴾ because of his disobedience and his embezzlement ﴿and his refuge is Hell, and what an evil destination﴾ the place of return it is.

﴿They are of degrees﴾, i.e., possessors of degrees ﴿in the sight of Allah﴾, i.e., differing in ranks. So for whoever followed His good pleasure (riḍwān) there is reward, and for whoever incurred His wrath (sakhaṭ) there is punishment. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, so He will recompense them for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 164:

﴿Indeed, Allah conferred a favor upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves﴾ i.e., an Arab like them, so that they might understand from him and be honored by him, not an angel nor a non-Arab (ʿajamī). ﴿reciting to them His verses﴾ the Qur'an. ﴿and purifying them﴾ cleansing them from sins. ﴿and teaching them the Book﴾ the Qur'an. ﴿and wisdom﴾ the Sunnah. ﴿And indeed﴾ (the particle inna is here lightened, mukhaffafa) i.e., indeed they ﴿were before﴾ i.e., before his being sent ﴿in clear error﴾ manifest.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 165:

﴿Even when a calamity struck you﴾ at Uhud, the killing of seventy of you, ﴿though you had inflicted twice as much﴾ at Badr, the killing of seventy of them and the capture of seventy of them, ﴿you said﴾ in astonishment, ﴿"How is this?"﴾ meaning, "From where has this defeat come to us, when we are Muslims and the Messenger of God is among us?" The last clause is an interrogative of denial. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"It is from yourselves"﴾ because you abandoned the position, so you were forsaken. ﴿Indeed God is over all things omnipotent﴾, and among that is victory and its denial, and He has requited you for your disobedience.
"And whatever befell you on the day the two hosts met" at Uhud, "it was by the leave of Allah," by His will, "and that He might know" with the knowledge of manifestation "the believers" truly.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 167:

﴿And that He may make evident those who were hypocrites.﴾ And those who ﴿were told﴾, when they withdrew from the fighting, and they were ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions: ﴿"Come, fight in the way of Allah"﴾ against His enemy, ﴿or repel [the enemy]﴾ from us, the people, by increasing your numbers, if you will not fight. ﴿They said, "If we knew fighting, we would have followed you."﴾ That is, "we would have done it well." Allah said, denying them: ﴿They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith﴾ because of what they showed of forsaking the believers; and they had been nearer to faith before, in terms of the outward appearance. ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts.﴾ And if they had known fighting, they would not have followed you. ﴿And Allah knows best what they conceal﴾ of hypocrisy.

**﴿Those who﴾** is either a substitute (*badal*) for the preceding **"those who"** or a qualifying attribute (*na't*). **﴿said to their brothers﴾** in religion, **﴿and﴾** they **﴿sat back﴾** from **jihad** (struggle in the way of God, here meaning fighting in battle), **﴿had they obeyed us﴾**, i.e., the martyrs of Uhud, **or** our brothers who sat back with us, **﴿they would not have been killed﴾**. **﴿Say﴾** to them: **﴿Then avert from yourselves death, if you are truthful﴾**, in your claim that sitting back saves one from it.

Revealed concerning the martyrs: "And do not think of those who have been killed" (read with light or heavy emphasis) "in the way of Allah" (i.e., for the sake of His religion) "as dead. Rather," they are "alive with their Lord," their souls being in the crops of green birds that roam in Paradise wherever they wish, as is reported in the hadith. "They are provided for" (they eat from the fruits of Paradise).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 170:

﴿Joyful﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun in ﴿they are provided for﴾ ﴿with what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾ ﴿and﴾ they ﴿rejoice﴾, i.e., they are glad ﴿for those who have not yet joined them from behind them﴾, i.e., their brethren among the believers. And ﴿that﴾ (an) is substituted for ﴿those﴾, meaning, ﴿that⁠ there is no fear for them﴾, i.e., those who have not yet joined them, ﴿nor shall they grieve﴾ in the Hereafter. The meaning is: they rejoice in their own security and in their joy.

﴿They rejoice in a bounty﴾, meaning a reward, ﴿from Allah and grace﴾, meaning an increase upon it, ﴿and that﴾ (with the fatḥa, وَأَنَّ, it is coordinated, ʿaṭf (coordination) on نِعْمَة, "bounty"; with the kasra, وَإِنَّ, it begins a new sentence, isti'nāf (resumption)) ﴿Allah does not waste the reward of the believers﴾, rather He rewards them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 172:

﴿Those who﴾ is the subject (mubtada'). ﴿Answered the call of Allah and the Messenger﴾ — his call to go out to fight — when Abu Sufyan and his companions intended to return, they agreed with the Prophet (ﷺ) to meet at the market of Badr the following year, from the day of Uhud. ﴿After the wound had afflicted them﴾ at Uhud. The predicate (khabar) of the subject is ﴿for those among them who did good﴾ in obeying him ﴿and feared Allah﴾ by not opposing him, ﴿a great reward﴾, which is Paradise.

**﴿Those who﴾**, a substitute for the preceding "those who," or an adjectival clause. **﴿To whom the people said﴾**, i.e., Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud al-Ashja'i. **﴿Indeed the people﴾**, i.e., Abu Sufyan and his companions, **﴿have gathered against you﴾** the armies, **﴿in order to uproot you﴾**. **﴿So fear them﴾**, and do not go out to them. **﴿But that increased them﴾**, that statement, **﴿in faith﴾**, in affirmation of God and certainty. **﴿And they said, "God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian."﴾** He is the one who suffices us in their affair, **﴿the best Guardian﴾**, the one to whom affairs are entrusted. They went out with the Prophet (ﷺ) and reached the market of Badr, and God cast terror into the hearts of Abu Sufyan and his companions, so they did not come. They had merchandise with them, so they sold and profited.

﴿So they returned﴾ from Badr ﴿with favour from Allah and bounty﴾ with safety and profit, ﴿no harm had touched them﴾ of killing or wounding, ﴿and they followed the pleasure of Allah﴾ by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger in going out, ﴿and Allah is the possessor of great bounty﴾ upon those who obey Him.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 3, verse 175:

﴿Indeed, that﴾ i.e., the one who said to you that the people have gathered [against you]; ﴿is the Shaytan (Satan) who frightens﴾ the Shaytan frightens you ﴿his allies﴾ i.e., the disbelievers; ﴿so do not fear them, but fear Me﴾ in abandoning My command; ﴿if you are [truly] believers﴾ in truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 176:

﴿And let not﴾ (read as yaḥzunka with a ḍamma on the yā' and a kasra on the zāy, or with a fatḥa on the yā' and a ḍamma on the zāy, from aḥzanahu) ﴿those who hasten to disbelief﴾ (who fall into it quickly, through its support), and they are the people of Makkah or the hypocrites; meaning: do not be concerned about their disbelief. ﴿Indeed, they will never harm Allah at all﴾ by their action, and they only harm themselves. ﴿Allah intends not to give them a share﴾ (naṣīb) ﴿in the Hereafter﴾, meaning Paradise, and for this reason Allah has forsaken them. ﴿And for them is a great punishment﴾ in the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 177:

﴿Indeed, those who have exchanged disbelief for faith﴾ i.e., they took it in its place. ﴿Will never harm Allah in the least by their disbelief﴾. ﴿And they will have a painful punishment﴾ i.e., painful, causing pain.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 178:

﴿And let not those who disbelieve think﴾ (read with the ya' or the ta', i.e., "yahsabanna" or "tahsabanna") ﴿that Our postponing [punishment] for them is good for themselves.﴾ (i.e., Our granting them respite, ʾimlāʾ) ﴿Indeed, We give them respite﴾ (nuhlī, i.e., We allow them time) ﴿so that they may increase in sin﴾ (through the abundance of sins) ﴿And for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ (possessing humiliation in the Hereafter).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 179:

﴿God would not leave the believers﴾ [i.e., would not leave them] ﴿in the state you are in﴾, O people, ﴿regarding it﴾ [i.e., the mixing of the sincere with others], ﴿until He distinguishes﴾ [yamīz, read with light or intensive emphasis] ﴿the wicked﴾ [i.e., the hypocrite] ﴿from the good﴾ [i.e., the believer], ﴿by means of the arduous obligations that make this clear.﴾ So He did that on the Day of Uhud.

﴿God would not disclose to you the unseen﴾, so that you would recognize the hypocrite from others before the distinction. ﴿But God chooses﴾ [yajtabī, i.e., selects] ﴿from His messengers whom He wills﴾, so He informs him of His unseen, as He informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of the condition of the hypocrites.

﴿So believe in God and His messengers. And if you believe and fear God﴾ [i.e., hypocrisy].

"And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think" — read with ya' and ta' — "that it is good for them" (the verb is read with ya' or ta'). Al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti gloss: "that is, its zakat." "It" refers to their stinginess (bukhluhum), "good for them." The second object (maf'ul thani) is "good" (khayran), and the pronoun (huwa) refers to "the bounty" (al-fadl). The first object is their stinginess, understood as being placed before the relative pronoun (alladhina) when read with ta', and before the pronoun when read with ya'.

﴿Nay, it is bad for them. They will be made to wear, as a collar, that which they withheld, on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — that is, its zakat from wealth — by it being made into a serpent around their necks that bites them, as is related in the hadith.

﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾: He inherits them after their inhabitants perish.

﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾ — read with ta' or ya' — ﴿Well-Acquainted﴾, so He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 181:

﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich."﴾ They were the Jews; they said it when there was revealed ﴿Who is it that will loan Allah a goodly loan?﴾ and they said, "If Allah were rich, He would not have asked us to lend to Him." ﴿We will record﴾ We will order the recording of ﴿what they have said﴾ in the scrolls of their deeds, so that they may be recompensed for it. In another reading, with the yā' and in the passive voice (as yukatibu, "it will be recorded"), ﴿and﴾ We will record ﴿their killing﴾ in both the accusative and the nominative ﴿of the prophets without right, and We will say﴾ with the nūn and the yā' (i.e., Allah will say to them in the Hereafter, through the tongue of the angels), ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning.﴾ The Fire. And it will be said to them when they are cast into it.

That (punishment) is for what your hands have sent forward, and (it is) that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants, so that He would punish them without sin.

Note on the passage: "(ذَلِكَ)" points to the punishment, "bi-ma qaddamat aydikum" is the Qur'anic quotation (﴿بِما قَدَّمَتْ أيْدِيكُمْ﴾), and "bi-zallam" (one who is excessively unjust, "dhu zulm") is the form negated in "﴿لَيْسَ بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ﴾".

Translation:

﴿That (punishment) is for what your hands have sent forward,﴾ where "hands" is used to refer to the whole person, because most actions are carried out by them. ﴿And that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾, meaning not one who has injustice (dhu zulm), so that He would punish them without sin.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 183:

"Those who" is a qualifying description (na't) of "those" mentioned before it. "Who said" to Muhammad, "Indeed God has covenanted with us" in the Torah "that we should not believe in any messenger until he brings us a sacrifice (qurban) which fire consumes." So, "we will not believe you until you bring us it." The sacrifice is what is offered to draw near to God, such as camels and other things. For previously, a white fire came down from the sky and consumed it; otherwise it remained in its place. He made this covenant with the Children of Israel, except concerning the Messiah and Muhammad. "Say" to them, as a rebuke: "Messengers came to you before me with the clear proofs," meaning the miracles, "and with what you said," such as Zechariah and Yahya, "whom you killed." The address is to those in the time of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), even though the act was committed by their forefathers, since they were pleased with it. "Why then did you kill them, if you are truthful," in that you believe when the sacrifice comes?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 184:

﴿If they deny you, [O Muhammad], then [know that] messengers before you were denied, who came with clear proofs (al-bayyināt) [i.e., miracles], and the scriptures (al-zubur) and the Book (al-kitāb), such as the scrolls of Ibrahim; and in another reading the letter bāʾ is affirmed in both of them, [and] the illuminating (al-munīr) [Book], clear, which is the Torah and the Gospel. So be patient, as they were patient.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 185:

﴿Every soul shall taste death, and you will only be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning the recompense of your deeds. ﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise will have triumphed﴾, meaning he has attained his desired goal. ﴿And the life of this world is not but the enjoyment of delusion﴾, meaning the living in it is nothing but falsehood, which one enjoys for a little while, then it perishes.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 186:

﴿You will surely be tested﴾: the nun of the plural (nun al-raf') has been dropped because of the successive nuns, and the waw is the plural pronoun, which is joined to the preceding sakin (the two consonants coming together), [the original reading being] "لَتُخْتَبَرُنَّ" (latukhtabarunna, "you will surely be tested"). ﴿In your properties﴾ through the obligatory duties concerning them and the needs [they bring]; ﴿and your selves﴾ through acts of worship and affliction. ﴿And you will surely hear much hurt from those who were given the Scripture before you﴾: the Jews and the Christians; ﴿and from those who associate partners [with God]﴾: from the Arabs; ﴿[hurt] of abuse, slander, and amorous verses about your women [i.e., insults and derogatory poetry]﴾. ﴿But if you are patient﴾ over that, ﴿and fear God﴾ by performing the obligatory duties, ﴿then indeed that is of the steadfast resolve of affairs﴾, meaning: of the matters that are resolved upon because of their being obligatory.

(And) mention when Allah took the covenant (mithaq) of those who were given the Book, that is, the pledge upon them in the Torah, [saying], "You shall make it clear (layubayyinunnahu) to the people (lin-nas), and not conceal it (wa la yaktumunahu)," that is, the Book; the two verbs are read with the ya' and with the ta' (i.e., both yubayyinunahu/tubayyinunahu and yaktumunahu/taktumunahu are recited). "Then they cast it behind their backs," that is, they threw away the covenant, "and did not act upon it. And they sold it (wa-shtaraw bihi) for a small price," that is, they took in its place, "a small price" of the world, from their base people, by means of their leadership in knowledge; so they concealed it, fearing its loss to them. "Evil is what they sell," i.e., this purchase of theirs.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 3, verse 188:**

﴿Do not think﴾ with the *ta'* (تاء, the second-person-style reading) and the *ya'* (ياء, the third-person reading), ﴿those who rejoice in what they have done﴾, meaning in misleading people, ﴿and love to be praised for what they have not done﴾, meaning for holding fast to the truth, while they are in error. ﴿Do not think them﴾, in either reading, is an emphasis, ﴿safe from punishment﴾, meaning in a place where they escape ﴿from the punishment﴾ of the Hereafter. Rather, they are in a place where they will be tormented, which is Hell. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾, meaning one that causes pain in it. The two objects of *yahsab* (يَحْسَب, "he thinks") in the first clause are omitted and indicated by the two objects of the second clause, according to the reading with the *ya'*. According to the reading with the *ta'* (الفوقانية), only the second object is omitted.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 189:

﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ — the treasuries of rain, provision, plants and other things — ﴿and Allah is over all things Competent﴾ — and among this is the punishment of the disbelievers and the deliverance of the believers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 190:

﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ and what is in them of wonders, ﴿and the alternation of the night and the day﴾ by coming and going, and increase and decrease, ﴿are signs﴾ indications of His power, Exalted is He, ﴿for those of understanding﴾ for those possessing intellects.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 191:

﴿Those who﴾ is a qualifier (na't) of what precedes it, or a substitution (badal) for it. ﴿remember God, standing, sitting, and on their sides﴾ reclining, i.e., in every state. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that they pray in this manner, as far as they are able. ﴿And reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ so that they may draw evidence from it for the power of their Creator. They say: ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this﴾ creation which we see ﴿in vain﴾ (batilan), a state (hal), purposelessly; rather, it is a proof of the perfection of Your power. ﴿Glory be to You﴾ — exalting You above purposelessness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 192:

﴿Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit into the Fire﴾ to abide therein, ﴿You have certainly disgraced him﴾, i.e., humiliated him, ﴿and for the wrongdoers﴾ the disbelievers therein ﴿there are no helpers﴾ who would protect them from the punishment of Allah, exalted is He.

In it, the apparent noun (al-zahir, الظّاهِر) was put in place of the pronoun (al-mudmar, مَوْضِع المُضْمَر), to indicate that the disgrace is specific to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 193:

﴿Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith﴾ calling the people ﴿to faith﴾, i.e., to Him; and he is Muhammad, or the Qur'an. ﴿That﴾, i.e., ﴿Believe in your Lord,﴾ ﴿so we have believed﴾ in Him. ﴿Our Lord, forgive us our sins and remove﴾ (ḥuṭṭa, i.e., lower or lay down) ﴿from us our misdeeds,﴾ so do not make them manifest by punishing us for them. ﴿And cause us to die﴾ (iqbiḍ arwāḥanā, i.e., take our souls) ﴿with﴾ (fī jumlat, i.e., among the company of) ﴿the righteous﴾, the prophets, the righteous.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 194:

﴿Our Lord, and give us﴾ what You promised us ﴿through Your messengers﴾ of mercy and bounty. Their asking for this, although Your promise, exalted be You, is not broken, is a request that You make them among those who deserve it, because they were not certain that they deserved it. The repetition of "Our Lord" is for emphasis in humble supplication. ﴿And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed You do not break the appointment﴾, the promise of resurrection and recompense.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 195:

﴿So their Lord answered them﴾ (their supplication), ﴿that﴾ (i.e., saying) ﴿I will not allow to be lost the work of any worker among you, whether male or female, [each] of you being from the other﴾ (kā'in, "existing," "being") ﴿from the other﴾, i.e., males from females and vice versa. The clause is emphatic of what precedes it, meaning that they are equal in being recompensed for their deeds and in not having their deeds wasted. It was revealed when Umm Salamah said, "O Messenger of Allah, I do not hear anything mentioned about women in migration." ﴿So those who emigrated﴾ from Makkah to Madinah, ﴿and were expelled from their homes, and were harmed in My way﴾ (My religion), ﴿and fought﴾ (the disbelievers), ﴿and were killed﴾ (qutilū, read with the lighter and the heavier forms of the verb, and in another reading with the order of the verbs reversed), ﴿I will surely remit from them their misdeeds﴾, I will cover them with forgiveness, ﴿and surely admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ as a reward (thawāban) ﴿from Allah﴾ (the word thawāban is a verbal noun from the sense of la-ukaffiranna, emphasizing it). The shift from the first person singular in "from Allah" is an iltifāt (shift of grammatical person) away from speaking in the first person. ﴿And Allah has with Him the best reward﴾, the recompense.

It was revealed when the Muslims said, seeing the wealth of the enemies of God in comparison with our hardship: ﴿Let not the movement of those who disbelieve deceive you﴾ their going about, ﴿through the land﴾ in trade and gain.

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on 3:197:**

It is ﴿a little enjoyment﴾, which they enjoy briefly in this world, and then it perishes. ﴿Then their refuge is Jahannam, and what an evil resting-place﴾, the bed. ﴿هِيَ﴾ (it, referring to Hell).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 3, verse 198:

﴿But for those who fear their Lord, there are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein﴾ i.e., destined to eternal abiding ﴿therein as a welcome gift (nuzul)﴾ and this is what is prepared for a guest; it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) of "gardens," and the element governing it is the sense of the adverbial locative (zarf) ﴿from Allah. And what is with Allah﴾ of reward ﴿is better for the righteous (al-abrar)﴾ than the enjoyments of the world.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 199:

﴿And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah﴾ such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions, and al-Najashi, ﴿and [in] what has been revealed to you﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿and [in] what was revealed to them﴾ i.e., the Torah and the Gospel, ﴿humbly submissive to Allah﴾. This is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the pronoun in "yu'minu" (believe), with regard paid to the meaning of "min" (among), i.e., humble themselves, ﴿They do not exchange the verses of Allah﴾ which are with them in the Torah and the Gospel concerning the sending of the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿for a small price﴾ from the worldly life, by concealing them out of fear for their leadership, like the act of others among the Jews, ﴿those will have their reward﴾ the reward of their deeds ﴿with their Lord﴾. They will be given it twice, as is mentioned in al-Qasas. ﴿Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾; He will reckon the creatures within a span of half a day of the days of this world.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 3, verse 200:

﴿O you who have believed, be patient﴾ upon the acts of obedience and over the calamities, and restrain yourselves from the acts of disobedience, ﴿and endure﴾ the disbelievers, so that they do not become more steadfast than you, ﴿and be stationed (rabitu)﴾ — persist in jihad — ﴿and fear Allah﴾ in all your circumstances, ﴿that you may be successful﴾ — that you may win Paradise and be saved from the Fire.
